selection: All five 2018 topic cells were attempted first; after the 2018 database exact-version endpoint failed, the already-frozen 2020 database cell was additionally screened. No paper was replaced in the 20-paper cohort.
method: Targeted inspection of the original version's introduction, claims/results and limitation/future-work sections; not a claim that every page was independently annotated.

rows.source_basis: The paper reports TRANX results on four tasks and concludes that it is generalizable, extensible and effective. This screen found no specific untested, falsifiable future question in those sections; generalizing its tested claim would be a new question, not a source-stated one.

rows.source_locator: pp. 2, 10-11; contributions and section 5, Future Work
rows.source_basis: The paper proves fixed-parameter tractability for chordal graphs, but explicitly proposes a Set Cover FPT-reduction showing general graph metric repair is at least W[2]-hard; it presents this as future work, not a theorem already proved here.
rows.candidate_question: Is general graph metric repair W[2]-hard when parameterized by the number of modified edges, under the paper's graph and allowed-weight-change definitions?
rows.candidate_falsification: A valid FPT algorithm for the general problem under the same parameter/definitions would oppose the hardness conjecture, subject to standard complexity assumptions; a correct parameter-preserving W[2]-hardness reduction would directly support it.

rows.source_basis: The exact-version arXiv PDF and abstract endpoints returned an internal retrieval error on this attempt. Search-result metadata alone is not a full-text source screen.

rows.source_locator: pp. 1, 9; introduction and section 6, Problems and Challenges
rows.source_basis: This is explicitly a vision paper, not an implementation evaluation. It identifies maintaining the FD table under data updates and dynamic FD discovery as an open challenge.
rows.candidate_question: Can an in-database functional-dependency table be kept correct under base-table updates with lower update-plus-query cost than re-mining the dependencies after every update?
rows.candidate_falsification: On frozen update/query traces, an incremental implementation with incorrect FD answers or no measured cost advantage over a matched full re-mining baseline would not support the claim.

rows.source_locator: p. 6; Conclusion & Future Work, Accurate evaluation of utility
rows.source_basis: The review says utility estimates can be inaccurate for stealthy or insider attackers and explicitly calls for deep-learning-based mobile-crowdsensing security robust to those errors.
rows.candidate_question: Under stealthy or insider attacks, can a mobile-crowdsensing protection policy retain security utility when its online utility estimates are perturbed, versus a policy without robustness treatment?
rows.candidate_falsification: On a specified attack and estimation-error distribution, no improvement in measured security utility at matched protection cost would fail the proposed robustness benefit.

rows.source_locator: pp. 1, 6-7; abstract, threats to validity, conclusions and future work
rows.source_basis: The paper already compares weak-mutation, line, branch and random source-test generation and reports an advantage in its study. It explicitly leaves larger codebases and additional strategies for future work; the broad comparison is not an open question at cutoff.
rows.candidate_question: Does the weak-mutation source-test advantage in metamorphic testing persist on larger codebases at equal source-test budget, compared with line, branch and random generation?
rows.candidate_falsification: Across independent larger-codebase units at equal test budget, no replicated advantage in independently verified distinct fault detection would fail this narrower generalization; mutant kills alone are a proxy.
